_source: Official Toastmasters Pathways evaluation forms (purpose statements)

A Dramatic Talk.objective: Develop an entertaining, dramatic talk using emotional appeal, characterization, and plot structure.

Active Listening.objective: Demonstrate your ability to listen to what others say.

Bringing History to Life.objective: Take a historical event, figure, or moment and bring it to vivid life through dramatic storytelling and narrative structure.

Building a Social Media Presence.objective: Apply your understanding of social media to enhance an established or new social media presence.

Communicate Change.objective: Practice the skills needed to effectively communicate change to a group or organization.

Connect with Storytelling.objective: Practice using a story within a speech or giving a speech that is a story.

Connect with Your Audience.objective: Practice the skills needed to connect with an unfamiliar audience.

Create a Podcast.objective: Be introduced to the skills needed to organize and present a podcast.

Creating Effective Visual Aids.objective: Practice selecting and using a variety of visual aids during a speech.

Cross-Cultural Understanding.objective: Identify your own cultural identities and the stereotypes that impact others’ perceptions of him or her.

Deliver Social Speeches.objective: Practice delivering social speeches in front of club members.

Deliver Your Message with Humor.objective: Practice developing and presenting a longer humorous speech.

Develop Your Vision.objective: Develop a detailed vision for your personal life, professional life, or an organization.

Effective Body Language.objective: Deliver a speech with awareness of intentional and unintentional body language, as well as to learn, practice, and refine how he or she uses nonverbal communication when delivering a speech.

Engage Your Audience with Humor.objective: Determine their style of humor and apply it to a speech that centers around a central message.

Ethical Leadership.objective: Develop a clear understanding of your ethical framework and create an opportunity for others to hear about and discuss ethics in the member’s organization or community.

Evaluation and Feedback.objective: Present a speech on any topic, receive feedback, and apply the feedback to a second speech.

Focus on the Positive.objective: Practice being aware of your thoughts and feelings, as well as the impact of your responses on others.

Get Comfortable with Visual Aids.objective: Select visual aids that are appropriate for your message and the audience; use visual aids with ease and confidence to enhance audience understanding.

Get to the Point.objective: Deliver a clear, concise message with a well-defined purpose.

High Performance Leadership.objective: Apply your leadership and planning knowledge to develop a project plan, organize a guidance committee, and implement the plan with the help of a team.

How to Say It.objective: Select clear, accurate, descriptive, and short words, using precise arrangements and action-oriented verbs to effectively communicate your message.

Ice Breaker.objective: Introduce yourself to the club and learn the basic structure of a public speech.

Improvement Through Positive Coaching.objective: Develop and apply skills for coaching a fellow member or a person outside of Toastmasters who can benefit from your expertise.

Inspire Your Audience.objective: Practice writing and delivering a speech that inspires others.

Introduction to Toastmasters Mentoring.objective: Clearly define how Toastmasters envisions mentoring.

Introduction to Vocal Variety and Body L.objective: Practice using vocal variety or body language to enhance a speech.

Know Your Sense of Humor.objective: Understand your sense of humor. Recognize the elements of a humorous story.

Lead in Any Situation.objective: Apply the skills needed to successfully lead in a volunteer or other organization.

Leading in Difficult Situations.objective: Practice strategies for adjusting to unexpected changes to a finalized plan.

Leading in Your Volunteer Organization.objective: Apply the skills needed to successfully lead in a volunteer organization.

Leading Your Team.objective: Lead a small team to the completion of a project.

Lessons Learned.objective: Learn about and apply the skills needed to run a lessons learned meeting during a project or after its completion.

Let's Get Personal.objective: Tell a personal story from your own life experiences that is humorous or emotionally poignant.

Make Connections Through Networking.objective: Develop and practice a personal strategy for building connections through networking.

Make Them Laugh.objective: Prepare a humorous speech drawn from your own personal experience; deliver the speech using the humorously exaggerated style.

Manage Change.objective: Practice developing a change management plan.

Manage Online Meetings.objective: Practice facilitating an online meeting or leading a webinar.

Manage Projects Successfully.objective: Practice developing a plan, building a team, and fulfilling the plan with the help of your team.

Manage Successful Events.objective: Practice planning, organizing, leading, and implementing an event.

Managing a Difficult Audience.objective: Practice the skills needed to address audience challenges when he or she presents outside of the Toastmasters club.

Moderate a Panel Discussion.objective: Apply your skills as a public speaker and leader to facilitate a panel discussion.

Motivate Others.objective: Practice the skills needed to motivate team members through the completion of a project.

Negotiate the Best Outcome.objective: Learn about different types of negotiation and the strategies that can be used when negotiating.

Organise Your Speech.objective: Select an appropriate outline; make your message clear with supporting material; use appropriate transitions; create a strong opening and conclusion.

Organize Your Speech.objective: Select an appropriate outline; make your message clear with supporting material; use appropriate transitions; create a strong opening and conclusion.

Persuade with Power.objective: Present your viewpoint in a clear, compelling manner; persuade your listeners to adopt your viewpoint or ideas, or to take the action you request.

Persuasive Speaking.objective: Understand the types of persuasive speeches and deliver a persuasive speech at a club meeting.

Planning and Implementing.objective: Practice developing a plan and bringing that plan to fruition.

Prepare for an Interview.objective: Practice the skills needed to present yourself well in an interview.

Prepare to Speak Professionally.objective: Practice developing and presenting a longer speech.

Present a Proposal.objective: Practice developing and presenting a proposal.

Public Relations Strategies.objective: Practice the skills needed to effectively use public relations strategies for any group or situation.

Question-and-Answer Session.objective: Learn about and practice facilitating a question-and-answer session.

Reaching Consensus.objective: Work with a group to practice reaching consensus on any topic.

Research Your Topic.objective: Collect information about your topic from numerous sources, carefully support your points with specific facts, examples, and illustrations, and deliver your speech effectively.

Researching and Presenting.objective: Learn or review basic research methods and present a well- organized, well-researched speech on any topic.

Resources for Entertainment.objective: Draw entertainment material from sources other than personal experience; adapt your material for your audience and topic.

Speaking After Dinner.objective: Prepare and deliver an entertaining after-dinner speech on a specific theme or occasion; weave humor into your central message.

Successful Collaboration.objective: Be introduced to or review strategies for working in a collaborative group.

Team Building.objective: Practice the skills needed to build a cohesive team and host an event.

The Entertaining Speech.objective: Entertain the audience through the use of humor and/or dramatic elements; organize an entertaining speech for maximum impact.

The Folk Tale.objective: Tell a folk tale that is entertaining and carries a moral or lesson; use voice, body, and facial expression to bring characters to life.

The Ice Breaker.objective: Introduce yourself to the club and learn the basic structure of a public speech.

The Moral of the Story.objective: Tell an engaging story with a clear moral or practical lesson that inspires the audience.

The Power of Humor in an Impromptu Speec.objective: Develop their method for giving impromptu speeches and practice adapting rehearsed stories during a presentation.

The Touching Story.objective: Tell an emotionally touching story that connects with the audience's empathy and heart.

Understanding Conflict Resolution.objective: Develop or enhance your understanding of the steps and strategies to address conflict.

Understanding Emotional Intelligence.objective: Cultivate an understanding of how your emotions impact relationships. It is also designed to help the member identify how others’ emotions impact your emotional state.

Understanding Vocal Variety.objective: Practice using vocal variety to enhance a speech.

Understanding Your Communication Style.objective: Learn about different communication styles and identify your primary style.

Understanding Your Leadership Style.objective: Identify your primary leadership style or styles.

Using Descriptive Language.objective: Practice writing a speech with an emphasis on adding language to increase interest and impact.

Using Presentation Software.objective: Introduce or review basic presentation software strategies for creating and using slides to support or enhance a speech.

Vocal Variety.objective: Use voice volume, pitch, rate, and quality to reflect and add meaning and interest to your message.

Write a Compelling Blog.objective: Review or introduce the skills needed to write and maintain a blog.

Writing a Speech with Purpose.objective: Learn or review basic methods for writing a speech with a defined purpose and to present a well-organized speech on any topic.

Your Body Speaks.objective: Use body language, posture, gestures, facial expressions, and eye contact to convey your message clearly and enhance your speech.
